claim: Miller's 7 plus or minus 2 counts items, not bits; absolute-judgment channel capacity is a separate limit of about 2.6 bits (about 6.5 categories).
agent_test: Not an agent test; use as framing only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Recoding into named chunks raises content held under a fixed item count (Smith: 12 octal digits held = 24 to about 40 binary digits).
agent_test: Compare raw log vs named-summary state at equal tokens on a multi-step task; score final answer accuracy.

claim: The human capacity when rehearsal and grouping are blocked is about 3 to 5 chunks (Cowan), not 7; Miller's 7 reflects strategies.
agent_test: Cap items per step at 3-5 vs 9 at equal tokens.
audit_note: Cowan's article does not state 'Miller's 7 reflects strategies' in those words (it says rehearsal and grouping must be curtailed to see 3-5); the 3 to 5 limit is for young adults.

claim: A fixed-count chunk limit fails under strict serial scoring: pairs help only under lenient scoring, and complex-span vs simple-span gap is not explained by chunking.
agent_test: Score the agent strictly (exact order/slots) not leniently when testing chunking benefits.

claim: Chunk count in chess recall stays near 7 but chunk size and count rise with skill; chunking is not a flat fixed-slot list.
agent_test: Test whether larger named chunks (not more chunks) lift accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Experts keep an advantage on random material (Sala and Gobet 2017: r = .41, 24 studies in the meta-analysis, trim-and-fill r = .29; experts won 49 of 55 samples), contradicting Chase and Simon's 'no relation at all' (N = 3, not in the meta-analysis) and supporting many small chunks.
agent_test: None directly; implies domain-specific stored patterns matter, so test pattern library vs none.
audit_note: Chase and Simon PDF is a scan I could not read; the Sala and Gobet table lists Chase and Simon 1973 with N=3, not in meta-analysis, skill effect No. All other numbers match (note the 4 'sources' for the meta-analysis are one paper, and the paper is by Sala and Gobet).

claim: Chunk benefits are domain-specific: training WM or learning music/chess shows near-zero far transfer with active controls (0.03 to 0.05 SD).
agent_test: Do not expect a general summary skill to transfer; evaluate chunk memory per task family.

claim: Huge span gains (digit span 7 to almost 80) come from long-term retrieval structures, not a larger short-term window.
agent_test: Compare enlarged context vs retrieval of stored structure at equal tokens.

claim: Chunks of size 2 act like redintegration (no working space saved); larger chunks (3 words) act like compression with a cost.
schema_part: O#: summarise only when it compresses
agent_test: Vary summary compression ratio and measure accuracy and loss of detail.

claim: Visual WM holds 3 to 4 objects regardless of feature count, and capacity correlates with fluid intelligence (about 43 to 46% variance).
agent_test: None; human only.

claim: GPT-3.5 on n-back shows human-like decline, d' about 1 at n=3 in three of four verbal variants; GPT-4 higher; six small open models very low.
agent_test: Run n-back on the agent's backbone at n=1-5 to set max tracked items.

claim: The n-back limit is not fixed: Llama 3.1 70B handles up to 10-back (task acc 84.75%), and weak-model errors reflect task misunderstanding, not capacity.
agent_test: Check for task misunderstanding before reading n-back as capacity.

claim: LLM span far exceeds humans for forward recall (50 digits) but breaks at about 15 backward; capacity does not predict executive scores.
agent_test: Prefer code control over model manipulation of stored items.

claim: Accuracy falls with irrelevant or extra input far below the context limit (0.92 to 0.68 by 3000 tokens; 11 of 13 models below 50% of baseline at 32K on NoLiMa; 18 frontier models degrade in Context Rot) and length alone hurts even with perfect retrieval and masked distractors (13.9% to 85% drop).
agent_test: Same task with 1x vs 3x padding at equal tokens of useful content.

claim: Position matters, but only at moderate fill: relevant information in the middle is used worst (U-shape, GPT-3.5 drop over 20 points) when input is up to about 50% of the window; near the window limit primacy fades and a bias toward the end of the input dominates.
agent_test: Place the current subgoal at the end of the prompt vs the middle vs start+end at equal tokens, at 25% and 90% window fill.
audit_note: GPT-3.5 drop is stated as 'more than 20%' in Liu et al (worst case), a different model family from the Veseli 50%-window result; combined wording is fine.

claim: Proactive interference: retrieval of latest value falls log-linearly with stale updates, predicted by parameter count, not context window; telling the model to ignore helps little.
schema_part: memory: do not leave stale state in context
agent_test: Compare deleting superseded facts vs telling the model to ignore them vs masking, at equal remaining tokens.

claim: Multi-turn delivery loses about 39% vs one-shot, mostly unreliability.
schema_part: G#: program holds state, restate full problem
agent_test: Compare restated full state each step vs accumulating conversation.

claim: Models fail to track hidden state not written in context; writing state out (CoT) partly fixes it, except some GPT-4o versions.
agent_test: Compare written state ledger vs implicit tracking on update tasks.
audit_note: Only Huang et al supports the CoT fix (GPT-4o 2024-11-20 is the outlier, other 4o versions rise to 17-21%); Kim and Schuster tests entity tracking without CoT and shows code-pretrained GPT-3.5 does track.

claim: Hierarchical subgoal chunking with summaries doubles success (21 to 42, AgentBoard) while cutting context 35% (HiAgent, single paper, no ablation, unreplicated); later work shows plain deletion of old observations matches summaries in code agents.
agent_test: Replicate HiAgent-style trimming with our scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Gisting plus lookup extends effective context 3.5x to 20x; gist-only compression 85.53% on QuALITY.
agent_test: Gist plus re-read vs full context at equal tokens.
audit_note: 3.5-20x and the 85.53% figure are from ReadAgent only (85.53% is the gist compression rate, not accuracy); MemGPT is a different approach and does not support these numbers.

claim: Chunking-style prompt reformatting (binding each entity to its attribute in one unit) lifted Tracking Shuffled Objects by 35.4 points on text-davinci-002.
agent_test: Compare bound vs separated state formats on tracking tasks.

claim: Small models often do better with simple answer-only prompts than complex prompting; reasoning does not reliably raise WM span.
agent_test: Per-model check of whether the scaffold helps or hurts.

claim: No study directly tests Miller's 7 plus or minus 2 or spontaneous chunk formation in LLMs; the human numbers are analogy only.
agent_test: Run own capacity-vs-items sweep.

claim: Cognitive overload via stacked irrelevant tasks degrades answers and enables jailbreaks.
agent_test: Single task per step vs bundled.

claim: Attention dispersion may cause LLM WM limits (entropy rises with N, negatively correlated with accuracy), but only in small models, correlationally.
agent_test: None; mechanistic.

claim: Replacing old tool observations with a placeholder (rolling window of 10) halves agent cost and matches LLM summarization in solve rate on SWE-bench Verified (e.g. Qwen3-Coder 54.8 vs 53.8; Gemini 2.5 Flash 35.6 vs 36.0). Summaries lengthen runs by about 15%.
schema_part: memory/O#: prune old observations before summarising
agent_test: Compare placeholder pruning vs named-subgoal summaries at equal tokens on our scaffold.

claim: Untuned LLM summaries lose needed detail (AppWorld gpt-4.1: 56.0 uncompressed to 43.5); compression guidelines refined from failure cases recover 56.5 at about 26% fewer peak tokens; too small a threshold costs accuracy, moderate is best.
schema_part: O#: summarise with rules built from failure analysis
agent_test: Sweep the compression threshold; log which facts were lost in failures and add them to the summary rule.

claim: Length alone hurts: even with perfect retrieval, whitespace or masked distractors, accuracy falls 13.9% to 85% as input grows; reciting the evidence before solving recovers part of it (GPT-4o up to +4% on RULER).
schema_part: G#: restate needed state before reasoning
agent_test: Add a restate-the-needed-facts step and measure it at 1x and 5x padding.

claim: Restating all prior information every turn recovers only 15-20% of the multi-turn loss (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini); a code-held ledger has not been tested.
agent_test: Run a code-held state ledger vs conversation accumulation on our multi-turn tasks.

claim: Chunking reduces load for other items, not only for itself, when chunks are retrieved from long-term memory, are non-overlapping, and come early in the list (Thalmann et al. 2019, abstract level).
schema_part: S#: put stable named chunks first in the prompt
agent_test: Put the stable chunks first vs last in the prompt and measure accuracy on the remaining items.

claim: Expert recall may rest on only about 2 to 3 large template chunks (Gobet and Clarkson 2004; masters up to 15 pieces per chunk), so a cap of 3 to 5 items per step should count large named structures, not atoms.
schema_part: G#: cap working set per step
agent_test: Cap by structures (2, 4, 8) at equal tokens and see where accuracy drops.

claim: Stored reusable workflows lifted GPT-4 WebArena success 23.5 to 35.5 with 2 fewer steps (Agent Workflow Memory), but no equal-token comparison against a longer context exists.
agent_test: Compare a library of 3 workflows vs the same tokens of raw history.

claim: A bounded rewritten state beats a growing history at long horizons: MEM1-7B (RL trained) reaches 3.5x the performance of Qwen2.5-14B full context with 27.1% of peak tokens at 16 objectives; training-free summarization gains only 4.5% (ReSum).
agent_test: Training-free bounded state vs full context at 16+ steps.

claim: Baddeley and Hitch (1974) dual-task numbers were not obtained; no claim from them is supported yet.
agent_test: Open the chapter or a secondary source with the digit-load table before citing.
